title: Ion Drive Shader Reactor Console
description: The user operates a reactor console where the BoxAnimated serves as a containment core and the PrimaryIonDrive is the engine being powered. By adjusting shader parameters through sliders and clicking interaction points, the user channels energy from the core into the drive, managing heat dissipation, plasma frequency, and chromatic aberration effects while maintaining energy conservation between systems. Undo/redo buttons allow reverting shader state changes.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing an interactive shader reactor console. Load BoxAnimated.glb on the left as the energy containment core and PrimaryIonDrive.glb on the right as the engine. Use OrbitControls for camera navigation, starting at position (0,2,6) looking at origin. Add ambient light (0.3) and two point lights. Create custom ShaderMaterial for both models using onBeforeCompile or replacement materials: the Box gets a pulsing energy glow shader with uniforms for pulseSpeed, glowIntensity, and hue shift; the IonDrive gets a plasma flow shader with uniforms for flowRate, plasmaColor, and distortionStrength. Implement an energy conservation system: total energy is fixed at 100 units. A UI panel has 5 sliders: corePulseRate (0-100), coreGlowPower (0-100), driveFlowSpeed (0-100), drivePlasmaIntensity (0-100), and chromaticAberration (0-20). Each slider costs energy proportional to its value. Display remaining energy budget; sliders auto-clamp so total never exceeds 100. Add 3 clickable hotspot spheres on the models that toggle shader modes (wireframe overlay, fresnel rim, noise displacement) each costing 5 energy. Implement a full undo/redo system: every slider change or hotspot click pushes state onto an undo stack. Undo and Redo buttons restore previous shader uniform states. The Box animation should play and its speed couples to corePulseRate. A post-processing UnrealBloomPass should respond to total drive energy. The interaction requires 10-14 steps: adjust 5 sliders, click 3 hotspots, undo 2 changes, redo 1, then fine-tune a slider to balance the system. Show a status bar indicating system stability percentage based on how evenly energy is distributed. Use dat.gui or plain HTML controls overlaid on the canvas.
